audit_findings.title: The cash bridge may treat customer-funded operating cash as excess cash
audit_findings.magnitude: $186.110m maximum bridge exposure, equal to $3.11 per share; deferred revenue was $343.208m
audit_findings.mechanism: Potentially reduces the cash bridge and, if servicing advance payments is omitted, future owner earnings
audit_findings.evidence: Deferred revenue mainly represents amounts collected prior to having fully satisfied cloud subscriptions, maintenance and professional services performance obligations.
audit_findings.explanation: This is an unresolved cash-classification possibility, not a demonstrated error: deferred revenue does not establish how much cash is operationally required, and forecast margins may already capture service costs. Even removing the entire $186.110m cash bridge reduces base value only from $47.47 to $44.36 per share and bull value from $55.43 to $52.32, still far below the $213.77 market price.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile June 2026 cash to deferred revenue and other operating liabilities, document the minimum operating-cash requirement and forecast treatment of fulfillment costs, then rerun the bridge using only demonstrated excess cash.

audit_findings.title: Unreserved securities and derivative litigation could create a senior cash claim
audit_findings.mechanism: An uninsured settlement, judgment, deductible, or defense cost would reduce the equity bridge or future owner earnings
audit_findings.evidence: We are unable to predict the ultimate timing or outcome of, or reasonably estimate the possible losses or a range of possible losses resulting from, these proceedings.
audit_findings.explanation: The proceedings and possible insurance coverage are demonstrated, but a loss is not. The company cannot estimate losses, and the record gives no insurance limits, deductibles, exclusions, or defense-cost terms. The claim may affect value, but the available record cannot establish materiality.
audit_findings.action: Obtain docket developments through September 5, 2026 and the applicable D&O policy limits, deductibles, exclusions, erosion by defense costs, and any accrual; rerun the bridge and owner earnings under supported litigation-loss scenarios.

audit_findings.title: The earnings history contains material nonrecurring 2025 items
audit_findings.magnitude: $13.8m favorable insurance adjustment versus $3.8m signing-bonus and recruiting costs, a computed net $10.0m pretax benefit; $6.5m SBC must remain
audit_findings.mechanism: Normalization changes the 2025 owner-earnings observation and therefore the fitted log-trend anchor
audit_findings.evidence: General and administrative expenses increased $4.0 million in 2025 due to a $3.0 million signing bonus, $0.8 million in recruiting fees, and $6.5 million of stock compensation expense related to the hiring of our new chief executive officer; a $5.4 million increase in compensation and other personnel-related expenses, a $1.5 million increase in professional expense, and a $0.8 million increase in office expense, partially offset by a $13.8 million decrease in expense related to an unusual health insurance claim as the final payment was much lower than the cost estimates previously provided by our health insurance provider.
audit_findings.explanation: The opposing nonrecurring items are demonstrated. Their identified net effect favors reported 2025 earnings, although the required retention of SBC and tax effects prevent treating $10.0m as an exact owner-earnings correction. Even an intentionally conservative, un-tax-affected $10.0m direct reduction to the $178.9m anchor would lower base value by about $2.48 per share; an actual ten-year trend refit should transmit only part of a one-year adjustment. This cannot close the gap between the $55.43 bull value and the $213.77 price.
audit_findings.action: Normalize the $13.8m insurance adjustment and the $3.8m cash hiring costs, retain all $6.5m of SBC, apply supported tax effects, refit the full log trend, and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: The India tax holiday expires inside the explicit forecast period
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed 2025 benefit of $4.244m, or $0.05 per diluted share
audit_findings.mechanism: Expiration after March 2029 reduces forecast after-tax owner earnings and terminal-value inputs if the higher tax burden is omitted
audit_findings.evidence: We currently have a tax holiday in India under the Special Economic Zone Act through March 2029.
audit_findings.explanation: The expiration is a known forward-looking change, while the filing quantifies only the 2025 benefit—not the post-2029 tax step-up. It should be monitored and explicitly modeled because uninterrupted growth could otherwise carry the historical benefit beyond its legal term.
audit_findings.action: Estimate post-holiday Indian taxable income and applicable tax rates, then rerun owner earnings from April 2029 onward and propagate the change through terminal value.

audit_findings.title: Gross cash may carry an unrecognized repatriation haircut
audit_findings.magnitude: $110.8m of June 2026 cash was held by foreign subsidiaries, equal to a maximum face-value exposure of $1.85 per share; actual haircut unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Local withholding or access costs would reduce the cash added in the equity bridge
audit_findings.evidence: As the undistributed earnings and profits are considered to be permanently reinvested, no provision for local withholdings taxes have been provided, however, upon repatriation of those earnings, in the form of dividends, we could be subject to additional local withholding taxes.
audit_findings.explanation: A withholding liability is possible but not demonstrated because neither the relevant jurisdictions nor rates are supplied. Even the extreme assumption that all $110.8m of foreign cash has zero equity value would reduce base value only from $47.47 to $45.62 per share and bull value to $53.58, leaving the valuation conclusion unchanged relative to the $213.77 price.
audit_findings.action: Map foreign cash and permanently reinvested earnings by jurisdiction, determine unavoidable withholding and access costs, and rerun the bridge with the supported after-tax amount.
